prerequisites: Knowledge of physics, calculus, and differential equations that the student will have acquired by taking the corresponding degree courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Students must have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students must have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.

syllabus_topics: BLOQUE 1. Introduction and basic concepts for nuclear engineering
Tema 1. Nuclear technology and its context
Estructura de la materia y formas de energía
Naturaleza atómica y nuclear de la materia
Tema 3. Interaction of radiation with matter
Interacción de los rayos X y gamma con la materia
Tasas de reacción con un flujo de neutrones polienergético
Tema 4. Effects of radiation on matter
Efectos de la radiación en los materiales
Efectos biológicos de las radiaciones ionizantes
BLOQUE 2. Energy applications of nuclear engineering
Factor de multiplicación. Criticidad y reactividad
Evolución temporal de la población neutrónica. Período del reactor
Descripción de las etapas del ciclo de combustible
Tema 7. Nuclear safety, radiological protection, waste and proliferation
BLOQUE 3. Non-energy applications of nuclear engineering
Fundamentos de la aceleración de partículas
Esquemas prácticos de la aceleración de partículas
Tema 9. Uses and industrial production of ionizing radiation
Tema 10. Medical applications of ionizing radiation
Tema 11. Radiation detection and measurement systems
teaching_methods: Independent study (studying notes, solving exercises, viewing support material)
Work with practical content (attending tutorials, participating in forums, in-person practical sessions)
Completion of assessment activities (continuous assessment tests, final in-person exam)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.1 × PraP + 0.1 × PEC + 0.8 × PruP. To pass, a global score of 5 or higher is required, and a minimum of 5 out of 10 must be obtained in each activity (PraP, PEC, PruP). If the in-person exam score is less than 4, the final grade will be the exam score, without weighting the other activities. Resit opportunities for PECs are available for the September examination period.
